An inner product space is a [[vector space]] over $\mathbb{F}$ together with an [[inner product]] $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$.

== Example ==

Let $V = \mathbb{F}^n$, $u = (u_1, \ldots, u_n), v = (v_1, \ldots, v_n) \in \mathbb{F}^n$.

Define
$$
\langle u, v \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \overline{v}_i
$$

Then $(V, \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle)$ is an '''inner product space'''.

<blockquote>
For $\mathbb{F} = \mathbb{R}$, $\overline{v}_i=v_i$

$$
\langle u,v \rangle = u \cdot v = u_1 v_1 + \cdots + u_n v_n.
$$
</blockquote>

== Properties ==

* [[Cauchy-Schwarz inequality]]
* [[Triangle inequality#Generalisation to vector spaces|Triangle inequality]]
* [[Parallelogram law#Generalisation into vector spaces|Parallelogram law]]
